title: Map anchors
description: The sidecar beside a screen-art map, `assets/src/svg/screens/<name>.anchors.json`: where each level's stop is on the drawing, in the drawing's own viewBox, plus the insets and the projection the points were placed with. It carries coordinates and no names, because a shipped JSON is reachable by a player and the basis for each point lives in the art sheet that never ships (assets/style/map-canada.md section 6). UI code places markers at these coordinates without looking at the map, so the claims this schema cannot state are cross-checked by make validate-content (scripts/lib/screen-art.mjs): `svg` names the drawing the sidecar sits beside, `viewBox` is that drawing's viewBox, there is exactly one anchor per place game.config.json#/journey names (ADR-0069 §6: keyed on the journey, not on content/levels/, so a level document and its anchor land in their owners' own commits), every anchor lies in the viewBox, each inset's frame, window, locator and anchors nest as they claim, a stop is in at most one inset, each locator encloses exactly the main-map points of its own inset's stops, and no frame overlaps another frame or lies within one pin radius of a main-map pin (ADR-0069 §3.1-3.3), and every listed region id is an id in the drawing. Mirrored by MapAnchorsDocument in app/application/ports/map-anchors.ts, which the level select reads to place its pins (ADR-0008).

svg.description: Filename of the drawing this sidecar describes, which must sit beside it: `map-canada.svg` for `map-canada.anchors.json`. A filename, not a URL - the shipped URL is content-hashed by the UI build.

viewBox.description: The drawing's viewBox as [minX, minY, width, height]. Every coordinate in this file is in these units; validate-content checks it equals the SVG's own.

units.description: The coordinate convention in words, for a person reading the file.

anchors.description: One point per place on the journey, keyed by level id. validate-content requires exactly the ids game.config.json#/journey names (null slots take none) - a missing one is a stop the screen cannot place, an extra one is a stop the map does not show.

insets.description: The enlarged views, in drawing order (ADR-0069 §1). Absent means no inset; an empty array is refused, because an empty collection must not stand in for none (ADR-0024). Renamed from the single-object `inset`, so a document that still carries `inset` fails naming that property.

provincesAndTerritories.description: ISO 3166-2 codes the drawing carries as element ids, for a screen that inlines the SVG. validate-content checks each is an id in the drawing.

mapPoint.title: Map point
mapPoint.description: A point in the drawing's viewBox; origin top-left, y down.

mapRect.title: Map rectangle
mapRect.description: An axis-aligned rectangle in the drawing's viewBox.

mapInsetFrame.title: Map inset frame
mapInsetFrame.description: The inset card's outer rectangle and its corner radius.

mapInset.title: Map inset
mapInset.description: An enlarged view of stops too close to tell apart on the main map. `anchors` are in the viewBox too, inside `window`; each names a stop the main map anchors, and that main-map point lies inside `locator`. A stop is in at most one inset.

affine.description: This inset's own fit from projected metres to viewBox units. Each inset is its own fit, and one shared field cannot describe two (ADR-0069 §1).

mapAffine.title: Map affine transform
mapAffine.description: x = a*E + c, y = d*N + f, from projected metres to viewBox units, so a later point can be placed without re-deriving the fit.

mapProjection.title: Map projection
mapProjection.description: The projection the drawing and every anchor were placed with.
